ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening under FINTRAC, including domestic and foreign politically exposed persons; required screening against the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) SDN list, the United Nations Security Council sanctions list, and Canadian sanctions under the United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2, the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, and the Canadian Criminal Code; enhanced due diligence is triggered for high-risk jurisdictions, PEPs, and source-of-wealth anomalies; ongoing continuous monitoring is required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry via the Corporate Online Registry System (CORES) portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use the Latin alphabet acceptable to the Alberta Corporate Registry; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated and/or translated into English or French for registration; the resulting name must not be confusingly similar to any existing Alberta corporate name, trade name, or registered trademark; prescribed punctuation, numerals, and entity designators must be used, with the 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company' designator as applicable.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Canada (where use implies Crown or government authority)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of the notice, using a fresh name search report and a written submission demonstrating non-confusion and compliance with the Alberta Business Corporations Act; the registry's decision may then be challenged by judicial review in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Administrative Procedures and Jurisdiction Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. A-3.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a subscription box service provider provided the virtual office offers a physical street address in Alberta for service of process and is not merely a post-office box; the company must keep corporate records and tax records at a records address within Alberta, and the registered office must be staffed or capable of receiving legal documents during normal business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated at 5% within the first year for a low-risk, license-free recurring merchandising business; unannounced visits may occur upon CRA or FINTRAC compliance warrant, but routine administrative on-site inspection is not standard for this industry in Alberta.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended — Part 1 and ss. 12 to 19 (articles of incorporation and statutory filing protocol), s. 102 (registered office and records office), ss. 105 and 110 (first directors and board governance), together with the provincial corporate name regulations; the unlimited liability corporation (ULC) designation is reflected in the articles of incorporation and adherence to the unlimited-liability regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Companies Branch, Service Alberta (Ministry of Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction), Registrar of Corporations, Edmonton, Alberta; registered through the official online corporate registry portal (corporate-registry.service.alberta.ca).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 under the Business Corporations Act) filed electronically through the Alberta Corporate Registry, culminating in the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up or authorized capital is prescribed by the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); the ULC may be formed with nominal issued capital (typically one or more common shares of no par value). Alberta imposes no escrow or paid-in capital account for a private non-public ULC engaged in subscription-box merchandising; statutory escrow requirements arise only for prospectus-distributed securities, regulated financial institutions, or certain licensed industries, none of which apply to ISIC 4791 recurring physical subscription box commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, as the first board decision of the Corporation:
1. The founding subscriber's share subscription is accepted, and one thousand common shares without par value are issued for lawful consideration and recorded in the share register.
2. The registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [Alberta street address], Alberta, which shall also be the records office.
3. [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, each to serve at the pleasure of the board, with authority to open payment-processing accounts (Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net) and execute subscription-box vendor contracts.
4. The officers are authorized to complete all statutory filings, licensing, and ancillary registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Companies Branch (Service Alberta), via an accredited NUANS service provider or the online registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS preliminary search on the proposed distinct corporate name (e.g., 'ABC Subscription Box ULC') to verify availability and distinguishability under the Alberta corporate naming regulations. Ensure the name is not too similar to an existing registered name or a protected trade-mark. Submit the name reservation request electronically or in person, pay the search and reservation fee, and retain the NUANS report priority number for the incorporation filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for confusion or a prohibited expression, revise the name with a new distinctive element (e.g., a coined or trade-mark suffix) and re-file the reservation; a cancellation or objection may be appealed to the Registrar within the statutory period, or the reservation may be renewed upon payment of the renewal fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation with ULC Designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Companies Branch, Registrar of Corporations (statutory review of the articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in English under the ABCA, specifying the corporate name, the registered office municipal address within Alberta, the first directors (at least one individual), the authorized share structure, and the ULC unlimited-liability designation. Execute the articles by each incorporator and obtain each first director's written consent to act. Attach the preferred NUANS report.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act of Each First Director
Notice of Registered Office and Records Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar identifies a deficiency in the articles (e.g., improper ULC designation or missing director consent), cure the deficiency and resubmit within the registry's response window; if the articles are rejected as confusingly worded, amend the operative clauses and refile with a corrected version, without requiring a new fee in most correction cases.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/register-your-business.html) and federal Business Number (BN) system; provincial tax administration for Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA under a tax collection agreement with the Government of Alberta.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an Alberta ULC must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and, where applicable, a GST/HST account by using CRA Business Registration Online or by completing and submitting Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) with the Alberta Certificate of Incorporation or registration documents. A non-resident registrant without a Canadian establishment may register under the streamlined non-resident procedure using Form GST20 (Request for Registration for the Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax for Non-Resident Individuals, Trusts and Partnerships), and the CRA may require security or a bond under subsection 240(2.1) of the Excise Tax Act where the non-resident does not have a place of business in Canada. The BN (9 digits) serves as the TIN for corporation tax, GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: For Canadian federal and Alberta income tax purposes the ULC is a resident taxable corporation and is taxed at the entity level (Entity_Level_Taxation), but it is eligible for disregarded-entity or partnership classification under the U.S. check-the-box rules (Treasury Reg. § 301.7701-3) because Alberta ULCs are not limited companies. The entity therefore carries dual-status classification: entity-level taxation domestically and elective transparency for U.S. tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) U.S. check-the-box election on IRS Form 8832 to treat the Alberta ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership rather than a corporation, which is recognized by the CRA for Canadian tax reporting of the resulting foreign tax attributes; (2) GST/HST streamlined registration election for non-residents under Form GST20, subject to CRA security requirements; (3) group election under Section 156 of the Excise Tax Act for nil-consideration supplies between closely related Canadian corporations, if applicable; (4) no domestic Canadian check-the-box election exists, and hybrid mismatch rules under sections 18.4 et seq. of the Income Tax Act (Canada) apply to any resulting deductibility/inclusion mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA); Alberta imposes no provincial retail sales tax, so only the 5% federal GST applies in Alberta (no HST provincial component).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies made in Canada over any four consecutive calendar quarters; however, a non-resident person that carries on business in Canada and makes taxable supplies in Canada is required to register unless the person is a small supplier, and the CRA may compel registration and require security for a non-resident registrant that does not have a fixed establishment or place of business in Canada (ETA subsections 240(1), 240(2) and 240(2.1)).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing clearance, or digital stamping regime under the ETA. CRA operates a voluntary e-invoicing framework aligned with the Peppol network through certified Digital Service Providers; GST/HST registrants must issue prescribed tax invoices containing the supplier's BN, transaction date, a description of the subscription box goods, GST charged (or a clear zero-rated indicator), and the registrant's GST/HST account number, and are required to retain invoices and supporting export evidence in a readable and accessible format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of tangible personal property (subscription box merchandise) is zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, section 1 of the Excise Tax Act where the recipient obtains the property outside Canada or the property is exported as soon as reasonably possible after the supply, and the supplier retains documentation establishing that the goods were exported within 30 days of delivery or within 60 days where the supplier holds conclusive export evidence; services performed on exported goods, and some services supplied to a non-resident recipient, may also qualify under ETA Schedule VI Part V sections 7-10 if the service relates to exported tangible personal property.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA ACI eManifest / B13A or equivalent electronic export declaration filed with the Canada Border Services Agency)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill showing Canada as origin and foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign currency receipt evidence (payment from non-resident card processor in FX)
Proof of foreign delivery (carrier tracking history, foreign customs clearance record, or signed delivery confirmation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where the required proof-of-export documentation is not obtained in a timely manner, the supply is retroactively re-characterized as taxable in Canada, and the CRA may assess unreported GST, disallow input tax credits, and apply interest on the net tax deficiency; intentional or grossly negligent conduct attracts a civil false-statement penalty equal to 50% of the understated net tax under ETA section 285.1, a minimum CAD 250 penalty under ETA section 280 for knowingly making a false statement or evading collection, summary-conviction fines up to CAD 25,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 12 months under ETA subsection 280(1), and potential director liability for unreported GST/HST under ETA section 323.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains fully liberalized current and capital account convertibility. The Canadian dollar (CAD) floats freely in global markets with no exchange control framework, no prior approval thresholds for foreign investment (except sector-specific national security reviews), and no restrictions on profit remittance, dividend repatriation, or capital repatriation. For an Alberta ULC, dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are permitted; the only applicable requirement is strict compliance with Part XIII Canadian withholding tax (currently 25% on gross dividends, treaty-reduced as applicable) and transfer pricing documentation. Remittances can be executed in CAD, USD, or any freely convertible currency at the commercial rate offered by Schedule I banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, mandatory conversion timeline, or repatriation timeline exists for export proceeds in Canada. Export receipts can be retained indefinitely in foreign currency, sold forward, or converted at the exporter’s commercial discretion. Every exporter must simply maintain adequate books and records for foreign currency transactions under the Income Tax Act (Canada), and the CRA may require the use of the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate for tax reporting purposes, but there is no regulatory obligation to convert export settlements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined federal (15%) and Alberta (8%) general corporate rate; a ULC eligible for and filing the partnership election is fiscally transparent and pays no entity-level corporate income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday or industry-specific preferential CIT rate for subscription-box merchandising. Standard incentives include the federal general rate reduction, investment tax credits for qualifying technology/media activities, and the 20-year carryforward of non-capital losses. The small business deduction is unavailable because a ULC with non-resident shareholders is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) My Business Account, Represent a Client, or certified tax preparation software; Alberta corporate income tax is integrated under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within six months after each taxation year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the deadline is June 30. Quarterly tax instalments are due on the 15th day of the month following each calendar quarter if the corporation's net tax exceeds CAD 3,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All worldwide subscription-box revenue, including monthly box subscriptions, one-time box purchases, shipping income, and ancillary product sales, reported in Canadian dollars and exclusive of GST/HST collected.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the ULC has elected partnership treatment, the T2 shows nil; revenue is allocated to non-resident members via T5013. Otherwise, report gross revenue and claim only deductions attributable to Canadian-source business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of procuring box merchandise, packaging, inbound and outbound freight, warehouse storage, and inventory adjustments calculated on a FIFO or weighted-average basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border related-party purchases must be recorded at arm's-length prices and reported on Form T106 if the aggregate controlled transaction value exceeds CAD 1,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as gross profit less operating expenses (advertising, fulfilment labour, technology costs, credit card processing, legal and accounting, amortization) plus other income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned ULC, only Canadian-source income is taxable absent a permanent establishment; any loss allocation to non-resident members is reported on T5013 and generally cannot offset non-Canadian income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta corporate tax is calculated on the same taxable income as the federal T2; the general Alberta rate is 8% for income not eligible for the small business deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the ULC is a partnership for tax purposes, no Alberta corporate tax is payable at the entity level; non-resident members may have Alberta Income Tax obligations through Part I or are subject to treaty protection based on business presence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance, plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months; a second late filing within three years increases the initial penalty to 10%. Daily compound interest is charged on assessed amounts. Failure to file Form T106 triggers CAD 100 per month, capped at CAD 2,500 for the first non-compliance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Statement of Partnership Income, filed through CRA My Business Account or commercial tax software, for an Alberta ULC that has made a valid election under Income Tax Act subsection 96(1) to be treated as a partnership.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar fiscal period the T5013 must be filed by March 31; for a non-calendar fiscal period, by the 15th day of the fifth month after the end of the fiscal period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports the ULC's full commercial revenue from subscription box operations, less cost of goods sold and operating expenses, yielding net business income or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The T5013 must allocate income or loss to each non-resident member in the year the income is recognized; the partnership does not pay tax, and non-resident members self-report or are subject to withholding under Part XIII where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income and losses according to the ULC agreement, including investing in goods, service, or limited partner capacities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident member, Canadian source business income is taxable only to the extent the partnership carries on business through a permanent establishment in Canada; if no permanent establishment exists, the member is generally not required to file Part I, but may still need to disclose the allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detail of opening inventory, merchandise purchases, freight, packaging, and closing inventory attributable to subscription-box fulfilment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident members may not directly deduct US inventory carrying costs unless connected to the Canadian partnership operations; transfer pricing rules apply to non-arm's-length purchases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of T5013 may result in a penalty of CAD 25 per month for each partner, to a maximum of CAD 250 per partner; repeat / deliberate non-filing can attract higher CRA penalties and gross-negligence sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory Canadian Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to non-residents. Under the Canada-US Income Tax Treaty, the rate is reduced to 15% for portfolio dividends and 5% for a corporate shareholder that owns at least 10% of the voting stock. A partnership-elected ULC does not pay dividends; instead, distributions to non-resident members follow partnership allocation rules and are not subject to Part XIII on distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must provide a signed Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty) to the Canadian payor in advance of distribution, supported by a valid Certificate of Residence (for US residents, IRS Form 6166). The payor must withhold at the treaty rate only if Form NR301 and the certificate are current and correct. On audit, the CRA will evaluate whether the shareholder is a 'qualified person' under the Canada-US Treaty Limitation-on-Benefits clause or has obtained discretionary relief from the competent authorities.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates are 25% for royalties and interest paid or credited to a non-resident. Domestic law exempts most arm's-length interest from withholding. Treaty rates: royalty withholding is generally 10% under the Canada-US treaty, with 0% for certain literary/copyright royalties; interest is generally fully exempt if the recipient is at arm's-length, otherwise 15%. Excessive or non-arm's-length royalties paid by a subscription-box company to a foreign related party may be recharacterized by the CRA as a dividend distribution.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate controlled transactions with non-arm's-length non-residents in a taxation year; this threshold triggers the mandatory Form T106 filing and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation. Canadian practice follows OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, and CRA expects Master File and Local File documentation to the extent that controlled transactions exceed this de minimis threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no separate annual Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) filing, but economic substance remains essential: CRA may apply the general anti-avoidance rule (section 245) to disregard tax-motivated transactions lacking commercial substance, and the Canada-US Treaty Limitation-on-Benefits clause requires substantive business operations, not a paper ULC shell. A subscription box ULC must demonstrate real employees, premises, inventory risk, and strategic decision-making in Canada to prevent treaty-shopping reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting subscription-box revenue received through Stripe Billing or Authorize.Net, destroying financial records, claiming fictitious fulfilment expenses, or failing to file T2/T5013 after invoicing customers in Canada and abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Act subsection 239(1): fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to five years. Civil reassessment, gross-negligence penalty under subsection 163(2) equal to 50% of the understated tax, plus compound daily interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who authorize or participate in evasion face personal fines, imprisonment, and civil restitution. In a ULC, shareholders also have unlimited liability for the company's tax debts; CRA may assert director liability for unremitted GST/HST and source deductions under subsection 227.1.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating and maintaining the Alberta ULC solely to benefit from the Canada-US tax treaty or partnership pass-through election, without physical office, employees, board meetings, inventory management, or revenue-producing activity; routing subscription box profits through the ULC to a tax-haven affiliate with minimal substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can invalidate the arrangement under the sham doctrine or section 245 GAAR, recharacterize the ULC's income as taxable dividends, deny foreign tax credits, apply subsection 163(2) penalties and interest, and impose Part XIII withholding tax on distributions that were previously treated as tax-transparent. Foreign courts may also deny treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a sham or substance-less ULC may be assessed personally for the corporation's unpaid tax liabilities; travel bans can be issued under CRA enforcement procedures for large assessments; directors face civil suits from minority shareholders or creditors, and the unlimited liability feature permits CRA to pierce the veil and pursue shareholders directly.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a subscription box business as a front to collect and transfer payments for third parties, accepting recurring payments without registering as a money services business, or failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports and Large Cash Transaction Reports despite processing prepaid or stored-value payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, administrative monetary penalties can reach CAD 500,000 per violation for non-compliance with registration, compliance program, record keeping, or transaction reporting requirements. Criminal money laundering is punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines at the discretion of the court.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers who knowingly participate in, or willfully fail to prevent, AML non-compliance can be prosecuted personally; the court may impose personal fines, issue compliance orders, and asset freezes. ULC shareholders remain liable for any resulting corporate penalties, and a conviction may lead to immigration inadmissibility and travel restrictions.
